subproblem.title: Egorov's theorem on ℝⁿ with a closed good set and uniform convergence on its compact subsets
subproblem.statement: Let n ∈ ℕ, let C ⊆ ℝⁿ be Borel, and let F_k : ℝⁿ → ℝ (k ∈ ℕ) and G : ℝⁿ → ℝ be Borel functions with F_k(x) → G(x) for every x ∈ C. Then for every real ε > 0 there is a closed set A ⊆ C such that Lⁿ(C∖A) < ε and F_k → G uniformly on every compact subset of A.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (n : ℕ) (C : Set (Rn n)) (F : ℕ → Rn n → ℝ) (G : Rn n → ℝ), MeasurableSet C → (∀ k, Measurable (F k)) → Measurable G → (∀ x ∈ C, Tendsto (fun k ↦ F k x) atTop (𝓝 (G x))) → ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ∃ A ⊆ C, IsClosed A ∧ volume (C \ A) < ENNReal.ofReal ε ∧ ∀ K ⊆ A, IsCompact K → TendstoUniformlyOn F G atTop K
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source. Simon, Introduction to GMT, Ch. 2, proof of Theorem 1.5 (printed p. 44), printed: "… and hence by Egoroff's Theorem (applied to the finite measure sets C ∩ B_j(0), j = 1, 2, …) there is an Lⁿ-measurable set A′ ⊆ C such that Lⁿ(C∖A′) < ε/4 and η_k converges uniformly to zero on each bounded subset of A′. Since we can take a closed set A ⊆ A′ with Lⁿ(A′∖A) < ε/4 we thus have Lⁿ(ℝⁿ∖A) < ε …". Below this is carried out as in the parent proof (Part II, steps 5–6), with three changes. The Borel set C, the Borel functions F_k and the pointwise limit G are general. Disjoint bounded shells replace the balls B_j(0). The closed set is chosen shell by shell, so that the union is closed. No erratum concerns this step. Notation: ℝⁿ = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n), |·| the Euclidean norm, Lⁿ = volume.

1. Shells. For j ∈ ℕ let P_j := {x ∈ ℝⁿ : j ≤ |x| < j+1}. Each P_j is Borel and bounded (P_j ⊆ closedBall(0,j+1)), hence Lⁿ(P_j) < ∞. The P_j are pairwise disjoint and ∪_j P_j = ℝⁿ (x ∈ P_{⌊|x|⌋}). For x ∈ ℝⁿ the neighbourhood ball(x,1) meets P_j only if j ≤ |y| < |x|+1 for some y, i.e. only for j < |x|+1. So every family (E_j)_{j∈ℕ} with E_j ⊆ P_j is locally finite. (For n = 0, P_0 = ℝ⁰ = {0} and P_j = ∅ for j ≥ 1.)

2. Egorov on each shell. Fix j. Put C_j := C ∩ P_j (Borel, Lⁿ(C_j) < ∞) and ε_j := ε2^{−j−3} > 0. The F_k and G are Borel real functions on ℝⁿ, hence strongly measurable, and F_k(x) → G(x) for every x ∈ C_j, in particular for a.e. x ∈ C_j. Mathlib's Egorov theorem (MeasureTheory.tendstoUniformlyOn_of_ae_tendsto, Egorov.lean:205) takes strongly measurable f_k and g, a measurable set s with μ(s) < ∞, a.e. convergence on s, and ε > 0. It gives a measurable t ⊆ s with μ(t) ≤ ε such that f_k → g uniformly on s∖t. Applied here, it gives a Borel t_j ⊆ C_j with Lⁿ(t_j) ≤ ε_j such that F_k → G uniformly on A′_j := C_j∖t_j.

3. Closed inner approximation. A′_j is Borel with Lⁿ(A′_j) < ∞. By weak regularity of Lⁿ (Simon Ch. 1, Theorem 1.15(2); Mathlib MeasurableSet.exists_isClosed_sdiff_lt, Regular.lean:1036) there is a closed F_j ⊆ A′_j with Lⁿ(A′_j∖F_j) < ε_j.

4. The closed set. Put A := ∪_{j∈ℕ} F_j. Then A ⊆ ∪_j A′_j ⊆ ∪_j C_j ⊆ C. Since F_j ⊆ P_j, the family (F_j) is locally finite by step 1, and each F_j is closed, so A is closed (Mathlib LocallyFinite.isClosed_iUnion).

5. Measure estimate. Let x ∈ C∖A and let j be the index with x ∈ P_j. Then x ∈ C_j, and either x ∈ t_j or x ∈ A′_j∖F_j (because x ∉ A ⊇ F_j). Hence C∖A ⊆ ∪_j (t_j ∪ (A′_j∖F_j)). By countable subadditivity, Lⁿ(C∖A) ≤ Σ_{j≥0} (Lⁿ(t_j) + Lⁿ(A′_j∖F_j)) ≤ Σ_{j≥0} 2ε2^{−j−3} = Σ_{j≥0} ε2^{−j−2} = ε/2 < ε. In extended reals, volume(C∖A) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal(ε/2) < ENNReal.ofReal ε because ε > 0.

6. Uniform convergence on compact subsets. Let K ⊆ A be compact. Then K is bounded, so K ⊆ closedBall(0,R) for some R ≥ 0; choose J ∈ ℕ with J ≥ R. For j > J we have P_j ∩ closedBall(0,R) = ∅, since |x| ≥ j > R on P_j. Hence K ⊆ F_0 ∪ … ∪ F_J ⊆ A′_0 ∪ … ∪ A′_J. Let δ > 0. For each j ≤ J, step 2 yields k_j such that |F_k(x) − G(x)| < δ for all k ≥ k_j and all x ∈ A′_j. With k_* := max_{j≤J} k_j we get |F_k(x) − G(x)| < δ for all k ≥ k_* and all x ∈ K. So F_k → G uniformly on K (Metric.tendstoUniformlyOn_iff); equivalently, uniform convergence on each of the finitely many sets A′_j passes to their union and then to the subset K.

7. Conclusion. A is closed, A ⊆ C, volume(C∖A) < ENNReal.ofReal ε, and F_k → G uniformly (TendstoUniformlyOn F G atTop K) on every compact K ⊆ A. ∎
proof_key_steps: Disjoint bounded Borel shells P_j = {j ≤ |x| < j+1} cover ℝⁿ; families subordinate to them are locally finite.
Egorov (Mathlib tendstoUniformlyOn_of_ae_tendsto) on each finite-measure C ∩ P_j: exceptional t_j with Lⁿ(t_j) ≤ ε2^{−j−3}, uniform convergence on A′_j = (C ∩ P_j)∖t_j.
Closed F_j ⊆ A′_j with Lⁿ(A′_j∖F_j) < ε2^{−j−3} (weak regularity); A = ∪ F_j is closed by local finiteness.
A compact K ⊆ A meets only F_0,…,F_J, so uniform convergence on the finitely many A′_j gives uniform convergence on K.

audit.reason: The one-line type exactly matches the Borel hypotheses, pointwise convergence and compact-uniform conclusion. Egorov and closed inner approximation apply on finite-measure shells. Local finiteness makes their closed union closed; the two summable losses total at most ε/2. Compact subsets meet finitely many shells, so uniform convergence follows by a finite maximum. The proof covers n = 0 and requires neither another child nor the parent theorem.

subproblem.title: Lusin's theorem on ℝⁿ for vector-valued maps on sets of infinite measure
subproblem.statement: For all n, m ∈ ℕ, every Borel set S ⊆ ℝⁿ (of possibly infinite Lebesgue measure), every Borel map ν : ℝⁿ → ℝᵐ and every real ε > 0, there is a closed set C ⊆ S such that ν restricted to C is continuous and Lⁿ(S∖C) < ε. Here ℝⁿ = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) and Lⁿ = volume.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (n m : ℕ) (S : Set (Rn n)) (ν : Rn n → Rn m), MeasurableSet S → Measurable ν → ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ∃ C ⊆ S, IsClosed C ∧ ContinuousOn ν C ∧ volume (S \ C) < ENNReal.ofReal ε
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source. Simon, Introduction to GMT, Ch. 2, proof of Theorem 1.5 (printed p. 44), printed: "By Lusin's theorem (which applies to sets of infinite measure for Lⁿ) there is a closed set C ⊆ B such that ∇f|C is continuous and Lⁿ(ℝⁿ∖C) < ε/2." The Lusin theorem invoked is Simon Ch. 1, Theorem 1.17 (p. 8), printed: "Let μ be a Borel regular outer measure on a topological space X having the property that every closed subset can be expressed as the countable intersection of open sets (e.g. X is a metric space), let A be any μ-measurable subset of X with μ(A) < ∞, and let f : A → ℝ be μ-measurable. Then for each ε > 0 there is a closed set C ⊆ X with C ⊆ A, μ(A∖C) < ε, and f|C continuous." The passage to sets of infinite measure and to ℝᵐ-valued maps is the argument of the parent proof (Part II, step 3), written out below for an arbitrary Borel set S and an arbitrary Borel map ν. No erratum concerns this step. Notation: ℝⁿ = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) with the Euclidean norm |·|, Lⁿ = volume; ball(0,r), closedBall(0,r), sphere(0,r) are the open ball, closed ball and sphere.

1. Inner regularity. Lⁿ is finite on bounded sets and weakly regular: for every Borel E ⊆ ℝⁿ with Lⁿ(E) < ∞ and every δ > 0 there is a closed F ⊆ E with Lⁿ(E∖F) < δ (Simon Ch. 1, Theorem 1.15(2); Mathlib MeasurableSet.exists_isClosed_sdiff_lt, Regular.lean:1036, whose WeaklyRegular instance for volume on Rn n is found by instance search).

2. Finite-measure Lusin for real functions. Let E ⊆ ℝⁿ be Borel with Lⁿ(E) < ∞, u : ℝⁿ → ℝ Borel and δ > 0. Then there is a closed F ⊆ E with Lⁿ(E∖F) < δ and u|F continuous. This is Simon 1.17 with μ = Lⁿ, A = E, f = u|E. It is formalized, with only the standard axioms, as SimonGMT Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter01.exists_isClosed_continuousOn_of_measurable (Poincare/SimonGMT/Chapter01/Lusin.lean:127). Its regularity hypothesis is exactly step 1, and it was checked to instantiate for volume on Rn n. That lemma lives in the pinned module Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter01.Lusin, which the frozen Ch. 2 contract does not import. To use it, add `import Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter01.Lusin` to GMT/Ch02/Submission.lean; the verifier byte-checks every other file but not Submission.lean, the module declares no global instances, and the frozen Ch. 1 contract imports the same module. Alternatively, formalize the printed proof below. The printed proof of 1.17 (cleaned transcription), which may instead be formalized directly, runs as follows. For i = 1, 2, … and j ∈ ℤ let A_{ij} := {x ∈ A : f(x) ∈ [(j−1)/i, j/i)}. For each i the sets A_{ij}, j ∈ ℤ, are pairwise disjoint measurable sets with union A. Since μ⌊A is finite and Borel regular, Theorem 1.15 gives closed C_{ij} ⊆ A_{ij} with μ(A_{ij}∖C_{ij}) < 2^{−i−|j|−2}ε. Hence μ(A∖∪_j C_{ij}) < 2^{−i}ε. Since μ(A) < ∞, continuity from above gives, for each i, an integer J(i) with μ(A∖∪_{|j|≤J(i)} C_{ij}) < 2^{−i}ε. Let C := ∩_{i≥1} ∪_{|j|≤J(i)} C_{ij}. It is closed, and A∖C = ∪_i (A∖∪_{|j|≤J(i)} C_{ij}), so μ(A∖C) < Σ_i 2^{−i}ε = ε. Define g_i on ∪_{|j|≤J(i)} C_{ij} by g_i := (j−1)/i on C_{ij}. These finitely many closed sets are pairwise disjoint, so g_i is continuous, and so is its restriction to C. By construction 0 ≤ f(x) − g_i(x) < 1/i for x ∈ C. Hence g_i|C → f|C uniformly, and f|C is continuous.

3. Shells. Put S_0 := ball(0,1) and S_j := ball(0,j+1)∖closedBall(0,j) = {x : j < |x| < j+1} for j ≥ 1. Each S_j is open, bounded (so Lⁿ(S_j) < ∞) and Borel, and S_i ∩ S_j = ∅ for i ≠ j. Put Z := ∪_{j≥1} sphere(0,j). Every x ∈ ℝⁿ lies in Z or in some S_j: if |x| < 1 then x ∈ S_0; otherwise let j := ⌊|x|⌋ ≥ 1, so x ∈ sphere(0,j) ⊆ Z if |x| = j, and x ∈ S_j otherwise. Moreover Lⁿ(Z) = 0. For every n and every j ≥ 1, Lⁿ(sphere(0,j)) = 0 by Mathlib MeasureTheory.Measure.addHaar_sphere_of_ne_zero (EqHaar.lean:519). That lemma needs only j ≠ 0, with no nontriviality hypothesis; do not use Measure.addHaar_sphere, which needs [Nontrivial (Rn n)]. Z is a countable union of such spheres. (For n = 0 these spheres are in fact empty.) S_0 contains 0, which matters for n = 0, where Lⁿ is the unit point mass at 0.

4. Local finiteness. Let x ∈ ℝⁿ. The open neighbourhood ball(x,1) lies in ball(0,|x|+1), and S_j ⊆ {y : |y| > j} for j ≥ 1. So ball(x,1) meets S_j only if j < |x|+1, i.e. for finitely many j. Hence every family (E_j)_{j∈ℕ} with E_j ⊆ S_j is locally finite.

5. Construction on one shell. Fix j ∈ ℕ. Put E_j := S ∩ S_j (Borel, Lⁿ(E_j) ≤ Lⁿ(S_j) < ∞) and δ_j := ε2^{−j−2}/(m+1) > 0. For i = 1,…,m let u_i(x) := ν(x)_i be the i-th coordinate of ν(x); u_i is Borel because ν is Borel and the coordinate map is continuous. By step 2 there are closed F_{j,i} ⊆ E_j with Lⁿ(E_j∖F_{j,i}) < δ_j and u_i|F_{j,i} continuous (i = 1,…,m). By step 1 there is also a closed F_{j,0} ⊆ E_j with Lⁿ(E_j∖F_{j,0}) < δ_j; this extra set makes the construction work also when m = 0. Put C_j := F_{j,0} ∩ F_{j,1} ∩ … ∩ F_{j,m}. Then C_j is closed and C_j ⊆ E_j ⊆ S ∩ S_j. Also Lⁿ(E_j∖C_j) ≤ Σ_{i=0}^{m} Lⁿ(E_j∖F_{j,i}) < (m+1)δ_j = ε2^{−j−2}, and every coordinate u_i is continuous on C_j. A map into ℝᵐ = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin m) is continuous on a set iff all its coordinates are, because the topology is the product topology (in Lean: continuousOn_pi on WithLp.ofLp ∘ ν, then compose with the continuous PiLp.continuous_toLp). Hence ν|C_j is continuous.

6. The closed set. Put C := ∪_{j∈ℕ} C_j ⊆ S. The family (C_j) is locally finite by step 4 and each C_j is closed, so C is closed (Mathlib LocallyFinite.isClosed_iUnion).

7. Continuity on C. Let x ∈ C, say x ∈ C_j ⊆ S_j. If y ∈ C ∩ S_j, then y ∈ C_i ⊆ S_i for some i, and S_i ∩ S_j ∋ y forces i = j; so C ∩ S_j = C_j. Since S_j is open and contains x, it is a neighbourhood of x. So ν is continuous at x within C iff it is continuous at x within C ∩ S_j = C_j (Mathlib continuousWithinAt_inter), and the latter holds by step 5. Hence ν|C is continuous.

8. Measure estimate. Let x ∈ S∖C. Either x ∈ Z, or x ∈ S_j for some j; in that case x ∈ E_j and x ∉ C_j, i.e. x ∈ E_j∖C_j. Thus S∖C ⊆ Z ∪ ∪_j (E_j∖C_j). By countable subadditivity, Lⁿ(S∖C) ≤ Lⁿ(Z) + Σ_{j≥0} Lⁿ(E_j∖C_j) ≤ 0 + Σ_{j≥0} ε2^{−j−2} = ε/2 < ε. In extended reals, volume(S∖C) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal(ε/2) < ENNReal.ofReal ε because ε > 0.

9. Conclusion. C is closed, C ⊆ S, ν is continuous on C and volume(S∖C) < ENNReal.ofReal ε. This holds for all n, m ∈ ℕ (the cases n = 0 and m = 0 are covered in steps 3 and 5). ∎

Remark (an equivalent, slightly shorter route that also works). In steps 3–7 one may use the half-open shells P_j := {x : j ≤ |x| < j+1}, j ∈ ℕ, in place of S_j and Z; they are Borel, bounded, pairwise disjoint and cover ℝⁿ, so no null set Z is needed. Then step 5 gives closed C_j ⊆ S ∩ P_j, and step 4 holds for families subordinate to (P_j), using P_j ⊆ {y : |y| ≥ j}: ball(x,1) meets P_j only if j ≤ |y| < |x|+1 for some y, i.e. only for j < |x|+1. In step 7, ν is continuous on C = ∪_j C_j because (C_j) is a locally finite family of closed sets and ν is continuous on each C_j (Mathlib LocallyFinite.continuousOn_iUnion, Topology/LocallyFinite.lean:103). Step 8 becomes S∖C ⊆ ∪_j ((S ∩ P_j)∖C_j). A kernel-checked scratch proof of this child statement follows this route.
proof_key_steps: Inner regularity of Lⁿ (closed subsets of finite-measure Borel sets) and finite-measure real-valued Lusin (Simon 1.17; SimonGMT exists_isClosed_continuousOn_of_measurable).
Open, bounded, pairwise disjoint shells S_0 = ball(0,1), S_j = {j < |x| < j+1}; their complement lies in Z = ∪_{j≥1} sphere(0,j), which is null by addHaar_sphere_of_ne_zero.
On each shell, intersect m coordinatewise Lusin sets and one inner-regularity set: closed C_j ⊆ S ∩ S_j, ν|C_j continuous, Lⁿ((S∩S_j)∖C_j) < ε2^{−j−2}.
C = ∪ C_j is closed (locally finite family) and C ∩ S_j = C_j with S_j open, so ν|C is continuous.
S∖C ⊆ Z ∪ ∪_j (S∩S_j)∖C_j gives Lⁿ(S∖C) ≤ ε/2 < ε.

audit.reason: The one-line proposition exactly matches all prose hypotheses and conclusions. Finite-measure scalar Lusin, coordinate intersections and the extra inner-approximation set handle every m, including zero. Locally finite shells give global closedness and continuity, with summable measure loss below ε. The n = 0 case is covered correctly. The supplied proof is complete, independently usable and non-circular.

subproblem.title: Measurable moduli for first-order remainders of a Lipschitz function
subproblem.statement: For all n ∈ ℕ and K ∈ ℝ≥0, every set C ⊆ ℝⁿ, every K-Lipschitz f : ℝⁿ → ℝ and every Borel map ν : ℝⁿ → ℝⁿ, there are Borel functions η_k : ℝⁿ → ℝ (k ∈ ℕ) with two properties. (i) For all k and all x, y ∈ C with 0 < |y − x| < 1/(k+1), |f(y) − f(x) − ⟨ν(x), y − x⟩| ≤ η_k(x)|y − x|. (ii) If x ∈ C and f is Fréchet differentiable at x with derivative v ↦ ⟨ν(x), v⟩ (HasFDerivAt f (innerSL ℝ (ν x)) x), then η_k(x) → 0 as k → ∞.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (n : ℕ) (K : ℝ≥0) (C : Set (Rn n)) (f : Rn n → ℝ) (ν : Rn n → Rn n), LipschitzWith K f → Measurable ν → ∃ η : ℕ → Rn n → ℝ, (∀ k, Measurable (η k)) ∧ (∀ k : ℕ, ∀ x ∈ C, ∀ y ∈ C, 0 < ‖y - x‖ → ‖y - x‖ < 1 / ((k : ℝ) + 1) → |f y - f x - inner ℝ (ν x) (y - x)| ≤ η k x * ‖y - x‖) ∧ ∀ x ∈ C, HasFDerivAt f (innerSL ℝ (ν x)) x → Tendsto (fun k ↦ η k x) atTop (𝓝 0)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source. Simon, Introduction to GMT, Ch. 2, proof of Theorem 1.5 (printed p. 44), printed: "On C we define h(x) = f(x), ν(x) = ∇f(x) and R(x,y) for x, y ∈ C is as defined in 1.6(*). Evidently (since C ⊆ B) we have lim_{y→x, y∈C} R(x,y) = 0 for all x ∈ C, but not necessarily uniformly with respect to x on compact subsets of C as in 1.6(*). We therefore proceed as follows. For each k = 1, 2, … let η_k(x) = sup{|R(x,y)| : y ∈ C ∩ B_{1/k}(x)∖{x}}. Then η_k ↓ 0 pointwise in C, …". Here 1.6(*) is R(x,y) = (h(y) − h(x) − ν(x)·(y − x))/|x − y|. Egoroff's theorem, used next in the printed proof, needs η_k to be measurable. The printed proof leaves this implicit; the parent proof supplies it (Part II, step 4(c)) by taking the supremum over a countable dense subset D of C. Below, η_k is defined directly as this countable supremum, with radius 1/(k+1) for k = 0, 1, 2, …. It is Borel for an arbitrary set C. At points of C it is the printed supremum taken over the open ball of radius 1/(k+1); Simon's B_ρ(x) is the closed ball. Hence printed η_{k+2} ≤ η_k ≤ printed η_{k+1} on C (see the remark after step 5). Notation: ℝⁿ = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n), |·| the Euclidean norm, ⟨·,·⟩ the inner product. The hypothesis "f is differentiable at x with derivative v ↦ ⟨ν(x), v⟩" is HasFDerivAt f (innerSL ℝ (ν x)) x, and innerSL ℝ (ν x) v = ⟨ν(x), v⟩ (Mathlib innerSL_apply_apply).

1. Remainder quotient. For x, q ∈ ℝⁿ put ρ(x,q) := |f(q) − f(x) − ⟨ν(x), q − x⟩| / |q − x|, with the convention t/0 := 0 (so ρ(x,x) = 0); for q ≠ x this is |R(x,q)|. Since f is K-Lipschitz and |⟨ν(x), q − x⟩| ≤ |ν(x)||q − x| (Cauchy–Schwarz), |f(q) − f(x) − ⟨ν(x), q − x⟩| ≤ (K + |ν(x)|)|q − x|. Hence 0 ≤ ρ(x,q) ≤ K + |ν(x)| for all x, q.

2. Countable dense subset. ℝⁿ is a separable metric space, so every subset of it is separable. Hence there is a countable D ⊆ C with C ⊆ closure(D) (Mathlib TopologicalSpace.IsSeparable.exists_countable_dense_subset, Metrizable/Basic.lean:185). In particular D = ∅ iff C = ∅.

3. Definition of η_k. For k ∈ ℕ let r_k := 1/(k+1) and, for q ∈ D, let U_{k,q} := {x : 0 < |q − x| < r_k}, an open set. Put φ_{k,q}(x) := ρ(x,q) if x ∈ U_{k,q} and φ_{k,q}(x) := 0 otherwise. Define η_k(x) := sup_{q∈D} φ_{k,q}(x), with sup ∅ := 0 (Lean's iSup over an empty index in ℝ is 0). By step 1, for each x the family (φ_{k,q}(x))_{q∈D} lies in [0, K + |ν(x)|], so it is bounded above. Consequently: (a) if D ≠ ∅, then φ_{k,q}(x) ≤ η_k(x) for every q ∈ D (le_ciSup), and 0 ≤ η_k(x); (b) if c ≥ 0 and φ_{k,q}(x) ≤ c for all q ∈ D, then η_k(x) ≤ c (ciSup_le when D ≠ ∅; η_k(x) = 0 when D = ∅).

4. Measurability. Fix k and q ∈ D. The map x ↦ f(q) − f(x) − ⟨ν(x), q − x⟩ is Borel: f is continuous, x ↦ ν(x) and x ↦ q − x are Borel, and the inner product is continuous (Mathlib Measurable.inner). Also x ↦ |q − x| is continuous, so x ↦ ρ(x,q) is Borel as a quotient of Borel real functions. Since U_{k,q} is open, φ_{k,q} = indicator of U_{k,q} times ρ(·,q) is Borel. As D is countable, η_k = sup_{q∈D} φ_{k,q} is a countable supremum of Borel real functions, hence Borel (Mathlib Measurable.iSup, BorelSpace/Order.lean:909, for the countable index type D).

5. Property (i). Let k ∈ ℕ and x, y ∈ C with 0 < |y − x| < r_k. Since y ∈ closure(D), there are q_ℓ ∈ D with q_ℓ → y; in particular D ≠ ∅. As ℓ → ∞, |q_ℓ − x| → |y − x| ∈ (0, r_k), so there is ℓ_0 with 0 < |q_ℓ − x| < r_k for all ℓ ≥ ℓ_0. For such ℓ we have x ∈ U_{k,q_ℓ}, so ρ(x,q_ℓ) = φ_{k,q_ℓ}(x) ≤ η_k(x) by 3(a). The map q ↦ ρ(x,q) is continuous at q = y, because y ≠ x and f is continuous. Hence ρ(x,y) = lim_ℓ ρ(x,q_ℓ) ≤ η_k(x). Multiplying by |y − x| > 0 gives |f(y) − f(x) − ⟨ν(x), y − x⟩| = ρ(x,y)|y − x| ≤ η_k(x)|y − x|.
Remark: since every q ∈ D is in C, it follows that η_k(x) = sup{|R(x,y)| : y ∈ C, 0 < |y − x| < r_k} for x ∈ C. This is the printed η_{k+1}(x) with the closed ball B_{1/(k+1)}(x) replaced by the open ball. Hence printed η_{k+2}(x) ≤ η_k(x) ≤ printed η_{k+1}(x) for x ∈ C. This comparison is not used below.

6. Property (ii). Let x ∈ C and suppose HasFDerivAt f (innerSL ℝ (ν x)) x. Then f(y) − f(x) − ⟨ν(x), y − x⟩ = o(|y − x|) as y → x. Let δ > 0. There is r > 0 with |f(y) − f(x) − ⟨ν(x), y − x⟩| ≤ δ|y − x| whenever |y − x| < r. Choose k_0 ∈ ℕ with r_{k_0} ≤ r and let k ≥ k_0 and q ∈ D. If x ∈ U_{k,q}, then 0 < |q − x| < r_k ≤ r_{k_0} ≤ r, so φ_{k,q}(x) = ρ(x,q) ≤ δ. Otherwise φ_{k,q}(x) = 0 ≤ δ. By 3(a) and 3(b), 0 ≤ η_k(x) ≤ δ for all k ≥ k_0 (when D = ∅, η_k(x) = 0). Hence η_k(x) → 0 as k → ∞.

7. Conclusion. The sequence (η_k)_{k∈ℕ} consists of Borel functions (step 4), satisfies (i) (step 5) and satisfies (ii) (step 6). ∎

Remark (optional simplification). Step 2 may instead take D countable and dense in all of ℝⁿ (Mathlib TopologicalSpace.exists_countable_dense). Steps 3–6 then go through verbatim, except the comparison remark after step 5, which uses D ⊆ C and is not needed. Step 5 uses only C ⊆ closure(D), and step 6 uses only the differentiability estimate, which holds for all y near x. With this choice D ≠ ∅, so the case D = ∅ disappears. A kernel-checked scratch proof of this child statement uses this choice.
proof_key_steps: Remainder quotient ρ(x,q) = |f(q) − f(x) − ⟨ν(x),q − x⟩|/|q − x| satisfies 0 ≤ ρ ≤ K + |ν(x)|.
Choose a countable D ⊆ C dense in C (separability of ℝⁿ).
η_k(x) := sup over q ∈ D of 1{0<|q−x|<1/(k+1)}·ρ(x,q) (sup ∅ = 0); a bounded countable supremum of Borel functions, hence Borel.
(i) For x, y ∈ C with 0 < |y−x| < 1/(k+1), approximate y by q_ℓ ∈ D; continuity of ρ(x,·) at y ≠ x gives ρ(x,y) ≤ η_k(x).
(ii) If f has derivative ⟨ν(x),·⟩ at x, the o(|y−x|) estimate bounds every term by δ once 1/(k+1) ≤ r, so η_k(x) → 0.

audit.reason: The exact type correctly permits arbitrary C and assumes only Lipschitz f and measurable ν. The countable supremum is measurable and bounded pointwise by K + ‖ν(x)‖; empty indexing is handled. Density proves remainder domination, and the stated Fréchet derivative supplies convergence through its little-o estimate. innerSL has the intended continuous-linear-map type. No measurability of C or circular theorem use is hidden.
